children.text: Contrary to popular belief, Shield Wall didn't actually get nerfed that much this league and is still going to be one of the strongest league starts, and arguably the best league start because of how extremely simple it is to gear in maps. In 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4, there have been a Smith of Kitava at the very top of the XP ladder the first few days (In 0.2 it was me :)).

The base damage nerfed on shield wall and fortifying cry was simply to compensate for the base armour buff on Shields. We will however do around 30% less damage at worst case against single target in endgame due to the Fortifying Cry changes which prevents it from shotgunning.

But Shield Wall was already exceptionally strong in 0.4 and the strongest build during the first weekend of the league. It was obliterating bosses already so a 30% nerf for single target might be warranted.
PASSIVE TREE CHANGES IN 0.5

For the be most part, just use the same tree as listed here for the 0.4 tree. If you want to try something new, grab vaal pact and the leech nodes that gives attack speed while leeching, these could be very strong. Note that instant life flasks should still work with Vaal pact (not tested), so an Olroth flask is very good if you go vaal pact.
REGEX:
to.att|speed|melee|leech|tower|Leech
When clearing:
Drop Shield Wall and either use a warcry or Shield Charge. Once you get to endgame, the more you can use Shield Charge, the faster your map clear is.
Against bosses
1. Freezing mark (can be skipped after you get armour break from other sources)
2. Place Totem
3. Infernal Cry + Fortifying Cry (When you get it)
4. Spam Shield Wall
5. Sunder after armour is broken (When you get Sunder)
6. Repeat

children.text: Shield Wall is not unlocked until lvl 22 unfortunately, so before that we will use Rolling slam + Boneshatter to clear and Perfect Strike after lvl 14 for Single target. Aim to get to lvl 14 right before fighting Count Geonor. Make sure you Talked to Leitis after killing the Executioner, she will then give you a guaranteed lvl 5 skill gem in town that you can use to cut Perfect Strike.
Rolling Slam + Boneshatter is a strong combo, but can take a little bit of practice to master.

Rolling slam has two slams built in, but you want to only do the first slam, then cancel the second slam by using Boneshatter before it. You can also control the rolling slam mid-attack by moving your mouse, which is sometimes useful, especially when rolling into a dangerous pack. You can then rolling slam into them from an angle to avoid getting hit by a bunch of attacks.

You can use a talisman on your swap if you want, but it's not super necessary, it will enable the usage of Pounce which helps you traverse the zones quicker. But this is more of a speedrunning tactic.

When you reach Act 2 you want to check the shops for a good Studded Greatclub to carry you until lvl 22. You also be on the lookout for a Shield with at least 80 armour, ideally more. And you wanna make sure yo pick up any Normal Body Armour that you can wear and put it in your stash, you will need it after you Ascend. The shop in town will update with new items every time you lvl up, so if you have yet to find a good shield, you might want to go back to town every now and then to check.

In act 2, we skip killing Balbala in Traitors Passage. She is very hard to kill with Perfect strike and even if you can, it's just not very efficient. We can get a guaranteed Barya in Deshar later on after we swapped to Shield Wall. Doing the Sekhemas Trial is so much easier with Shield Wall compared to Rolling Slam + Boneshatter and Perfect Strike.

After killing Jamanra the first time in Halani gates, we will get our first lvl 7 skill gem. This one we will use to cut Shield Wall. In order to guarantee a second lvl 7 skill gem, we do Mastodon Badlands area first, then we go to Keth. And in Keth the Snake boss will then always drop a lvl 7 skill gem, we use this to cut Freezing mark.

Freezing Mark, doesn't actually do anything for us, instead it's the support we use on it, Mark for Death (To break armour) and Mark of Siphoning (To Leech) that are valuable. You might be missing strength and dexterity attributes to immediately equip Freezing mark at lvl 22, this is normal.

If you are confident in your game play, you might have a Talisman and Pounce on a swap with the same supports which does not have that high attribute requirements. If you have a Talisman you can even use the second lvl 7 skill gem to cut Ferocious roar instead.

When you reach lvl 22 you want to go back to town respec your character into Shield Wall. At this point you should have a Shield with at least 80+ Armour and if you're lucky you might even have a one handed mace with + to melee skills (Base type and damage doesn't matter).
Go talk to the hooded one to respec some of your points, you want to remove all nodes in the Singular Purpose cluster, as we are not using two handed weapons anymore.
IMPORTANT:

Shield Wall damage scales off of the armour on your shield, which makes this the single most important modifier of your gear from now on. Typically the mace or other weapons you may use don't matter much, but there are a few global modifiers on the weapon that can boost the shield wall damage. In campaign it's mainly going to be + levels to melee.
In act 3 we will unlock Fortifying Cry and Sunder with our first T9 skill gems.
Exploding the Shield Walls with Fortifying Cry will Boost our damage slightly and give us a little bit of guard.
We use Sunder just to proc Sundered Armour on bosses after we break their armour, this will make the bosses take 40% increased physical damage taken instead of just 20%

In act 4 we get the enraged warcry support, which we'll slot into fortifying cry, which means we can completely ignore the cooldown if we have enough rage. Which we will always have at bosses for example.
When you reach maps, do the third ascendency immediately and grab the coal stoker node.

At this point you can just stack as much fire resistance as you can and you will cap all other resistances. This frees up so many mods on your gear that you can start stacking rarity before any other class.
You can also get a Thrillsteel helmet as soon as you can, this will increase your attack speed and movement speed.
The last lineage support you are looking for is Uul-Netol's Embrace, which gives a substantial amount of chaos damage, and it also break armour for you. So you can update the mace at this point.
